title: Week 8 Flow Drill
h1: Flow networks and maximum flow drill
footer: Written from the Week 8 lecture and lab. New network, not the practice quiz. The max flow and minimum cut were checked by running Edmonds-Karp in Python (revision/tools/flow_check.py).

sections.label: Section 1
sections.name: Valid flows, size and cuts
sections.figcap: Use this network for 1.1 to 1.5. Each label is flow/capacity.

qs.p: What is the size (value) of the flow shown?
qs.ex: Add the flows leaving S: S to A is 5 and S to B is 4, so 5 + 4 = 9. Check: entering T is 5 + 4 = 9. Option C adds up the capacities of the edges into T plus something else; option A only counts one edge.

qs.p: At vertex D, what are the total flow in and the total flow out?
qs.ex: In: only B to D carries 5. Out: D to C carries 1 and D to T carries 4, so 1 + 4 = 5. They are equal, so conservation holds at D. Option A uses the capacity 6 instead of the flow.

qs.p: Someone changes only the label on A to B from 1/3 to 2/3. Which rule is now broken?
opts: The capacity rule on A to B
Conservation at A and at B
No rule; the flow is still valid
qs.ex: 2 is still at most 3, so the capacity rule is fine. But A now has in 5 and out 2 + 4 = 6, and B has in 4 + 2 = 6 and out 5. In is not equal to out at A and B, so conservation is broken there. S and T never need conservation.

qs.p: What is the capacity of the cut with left side {S, B, D} and right side {A, C, T}?
qs.ex: Left to right edges: S to A (capacity 7), D to C (2), D to T (4). 7 + 2 + 4 = 13. A to B goes from the right side to the left side, so it is NOT counted. Counting it gives option B, 16. Use the capacities (second numbers), not the flows.

qs.p: The flow shown has size 9. The cut with left side {S, A, B, C, D} has capacity 5 + 4 = 9. What can you conclude?
opts: Nothing, because flows and cuts are unrelated
The flow could still be increased to 11
The flow is a maximum flow and this cut is a minimum cut
qs.ex: Every flow is at most every cut. A flow and a cut with the same number prove each other: the flow cannot go higher than 9, and no cut can be lower than 9. This is the max-flow min-cut theorem.

sections.label: Section 2
sections.name: Ford-Fulkerson, residual networks and Edmonds-Karp
sections.figcap: Use this network (capacities only, starting with zero flow) for 2.2 to 2.4.

qs.p: An edge A to B has the label 1/3 (flow 1, capacity 3). What are its residual capacities?
opts: Forward A to B is 2, reverse B to A is 1
Forward A to B is 1, reverse B to A is 2
Forward A to B is 3, reverse B to A is 0
Forward A to B is 2, reverse B to A is 3
qs.ex: Forward room is capacity minus flow: 3 − 1 = 2. Reverse room is the flow: 1, because up to 1 unit could be undone.

qs.p: Starting from zero flow, Ford-Fulkerson first picks the path S, A, C, T. What is its bottleneck?
qs.ex: Room on each edge: S to A is 7, A to C is 4, C to T is 5. The bottleneck is the smallest, 4. Option C adds them, which is wrong: the narrowest pipe limits the whole path.

qs.p: After pushing 4 along S, A, C, T and then 4 along S, B, D, T, the next path is S, A, B, D, C, T. What is its bottleneck, and what is the total flow after it?
qs.ex: Room left: S to A is 7 − 4 = 3, A to B is 3, B to D is 6 − 4 = 2, D to C is 2, C to T is 5 − 4 = 1. Smallest is 1. Total 4 + 4 + 1 = 9.

qs.p: What is the maximum flow from S to T in this network?
qs.ex: After the three paths in 2.3 the total is 9, and C to T (5) and D to T (4) are both full. That cut has capacity 5 + 4 = 9, so 9 is the maximum. Option C is the cut {S} alone (7 + 4 = 11), which is not the smallest cut.

qs.p: Which statement about Edmonds-Karp is TRUE?
opts: It picks the augmenting path with the largest bottleneck
It runs in O(m times f*) time, which depends on the capacities
It is Ford-Fulkerson using BFS, so each augmenting path has the fewest edges, and it runs in O(n m²)
qs.ex: Edmonds-Karp finds each augmenting path with BFS, giving the fewest edges, and runs in O(n m²) whatever the capacities are. O(m times f*) is plain Ford-Fulkerson. It does use reverse edges in the residual network.

qs.p: To solve bipartite matching (pairing workers with jobs) as a max flow problem, what capacity is given to every edge?
qs.ex: Add s joined to every worker and every job joined to t, and give every edge capacity 1. That way no worker or job can be used twice, and the max flow equals the size of the biggest matching.
